evidence.curator_note: Generic allylic cleavage of an alkene molecular ion, R-CH2-CH=CH2(+.) -> R. + CH2=CH-CH2(+), arrow labelled alpha. Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,2> are drawn -- one arc leaves the ionized C=C (the book prints '+.' over that linkage rather than on one atom) and one arc leaves the R-CH2 sigma bond, both landing on the CH2-CH bond that becomes the new double bond -- move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). DELOCALISATION: the ionized double bond is localised here as R-CH2-CH(.)-CH2(+) (odd electron on atom 3, charge on atom 4) so the drawn arcs have a real origin; the equivalent localisation R-CH2-CH(+)-CH2(.) would carry the same arcs mirrored. The allyl cation product is likewise delocalised and is written in the single form the book prints, CH2=CH-CH2(+). Instantiated by the curator as R = CH3 (1-butene molecular ion); the page prints no compound, no m/z and no intensity.

rule_index cross-links equation 4.12 to IMS_4_12_1 ([C]1[C]2[C]3[C+.]4 >> [C.]1.[C]2{=}[C]3[C+]4) and IMS_4_12_2 ([C]1[C]2[C+.]3[C]4 >> [C.]1.[C]2{=}[C]3[C+]4). VERIFIED MISMATCH, not support: both reactant patterns are all-single-bond carbon chains, so the alkene that defines allylic cleavage is not required at all, and both place charge AND odd electron on one carbon ([C+.]), which is not a localisation of an ionized C=C. Checked in the container: neither rule matches the localised 1-butene ion CH3-CH2-CH(.)-CH2(+), nor 1-butene with the C=C retained and a [C+.] terminus (the pipeline's own ei_molecular_ion form); both DO fire on SATURATED n-butane M+. and return C=[CH2][CH3+] -- a pentavalent CH2 and a tetravalent CH3+ -- so what they encode is an impossible cleavage of an alkane. They conserve charge and spin, so the guardrail keeps them live. m/z values here are curator-computed from the instantiation.

No m/z or intensity is printed for this generic scheme; 41.0386 is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of the allyl cation C3H5+ for the chosen 1-butene instantiation (electron-mass corrected). Not a measurement.
